Vicor — The power components maker's stock rose about 11%, on pace for its best day since July 30, after the company said it was acquiring two sites in New Hampshire for additional ChiP fab manufacturing. Shopify — Shares popped nearly 4% for the Canada-based commerce company after Bernstein initiated coverage for the stock and gave an outperform rating. The analysts gave a $160 price target, implying a 26% upside from Thursday's close and noted AI would expand rather than hurt the company's performance. Skyworks Solutions — Shares rose more than 8% after the semiconductor company said at a Goldman Sachs conference that it expects its acquisition of Qorvo to close before year-end. Qorvo shares advanced 5%. Qualys — The cybersecurity stock fell 6% following a downgrade at Wedbush to neutral from outperform. The firm said Qualys' core business is facing significant pressure. GameStop — Shares of the video game retailer and meme stock climbed nearly 3% after CEO Ryan Cohen disclosed he purchased 1 million shares at an average price of $20.375. Cohen now owns 39.347 million shares. As of Thursday's close, that stake was valued at around $802.28 million. Oracle — The software giant's stock was down slightly after its post-earnings rally fizzled. Shares rose as much as 10% after Oracle said it earned $1.92 per share on an adjusted basis and posted revenue of $19.35 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG sought $1.74 per share and $19.14 billion. RH — Shares of the home furnishings retailer rose almost 2%. RH posted second-quarter revenue of $922 million, beating the LSEG consensus call for $915 million. Full-year revenue guidance calls for growth in a range of 5.5% to 7%, while analysts sought a 5.6% increase. NuScale Power — The designer of small modular reactors' shares tumbled 14% after UBS downgraded the stock to sell from neutral, dialing back its price target to $6 from $10 and pointing to NuScale's long build timeline. Oklo — The nuclear power stock slid more than 7% after the company entered an at-the-market common stock sale agreement . — CNBC's Nick Wells contributed reporting.

The company saw strong growth in its cloud services, with cloud infrastructure revenue soaring. Oracle has been raising debt to fund its AI data center buildout. In this article ORCL SPCX SAP Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Oracle Corp. signage on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, US, on Wednesday, Aug. 12, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Oracle shares whipsawed on Friday after the software company reported 30% revenue growth for the latest quarter, topping estimates, with sales fueled by strong demand for cloud infrastructure. The stock popped after the open before sinking back to near flat. Fiscal first-quarter revenue increased to $19.35 billion, beating LSEG consensus estimates of $19.14 billion. Net income climbed 60% to $4.7 billion from $2.93 billion in the prior year. Cloud revenue rose 62% from a year earlier to $11.6 billion, driven by a 121% jump in cloud infrastructure revenue, while cloud application revenue grew 10%. Even with Friday's rally, Oracle is down about 20% this year on concern about the hefty amount of debt the company has raised to fund its artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout. Oracle stock chart Oracle delivered an additional 850 megawatts of data center capacity in the quarter. It also booked over $30 billion in further AI cloud contracts, and delivered more than 300,000 graphics processing units to its AI Cloud customers. The company guided to second-quarter revenue growth of 30% to 34%, with cloud revenue rising between 64% and 70%. It expects total revenue for the 2027 fiscal year to be at least $90 billion. Alongside selling its flagship database software, Oracle now has $125 billion in debt as it funds an expansive buildout of data centers for AI workloads. The investment is expected to expand capacity for contracted cloud demand from customers including Nvidia, Meta, OpenAI, Advanced Micro Devices and SpaceX's AI business. Oracle posted $5.4 billion in negative free cash flow during the quarter, versus a negative $362 million a year earlier. A 'solid' quarter Citi analysts reiterated their buy rating in a Friday note, saying Oracle had met expectations and "cleared the runway" for its upcoming investor day. "Oracle delivered a solid fiscal first quarter that checked nearly every box and reinforces the bull case," the analysts wrote. Oracle's outlook for 2027 is "modest," and the company's management framework is "conservative," the analysts said.
